description: I'm Nivitha and I'm a BTech undergrad. This is my first time participating in a global hackathone.
summary:
For the NASA's Space Apps Challenge, I've developed an engaging, age-appropriate educational story and visual pitch, specifically tailored for 10-year-old learners.
The project addresses the challenges by translating complex technical records, authentic Apollo Mission Archives, and Perseverance Rover missions Of NASA into a captivating narrative. 

Rather than viewing leftover spacecraft equipment as space trash, the story illustrates how materials like aluminized thermal gold foil and titanium landing gear protected astronauts and made safe landings possible on Moon and Mars, and why heavy items had to be left behind for the return trip.

This project inspires scientific curiosity and literacy in young minds by turning historical space artefacts into a living legacy. By highlighting how abandoned gear such as lunar laser still actively help scientists measure the Moon's drift from Earth over 50 years later, the project shows kids that human engineering and exploration leave a lasting meaningful mark on the universe.
details:
This is an interactive, visually driven educational storytelling presentation built on 11 slides of Google Slides deck. It translates dense aerospace engineering concepts and historical mission logs into fun relatable analogies (such as comparing gold thermal insulation to "space-sunglasses") that 10-year-olds can immediately grasp.

By combining concise slide copy with strong visual storytelling, the deck avoids information overload and holds the attention of young learners within strict presentation limits.

The primary goal of this project is to shift how young audiences view space history; rebranding leftover Lunar and Mars equipment from discarded space trash into an active, living scientific legacy.

Google Slides was used to structure, design and format the 11-slide visual pitch deck.

NASA's public open data portal, including historical Apollo Technical Documentation, mission photo archives, and high-resolution imagery from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.

AI-assisted brainstorming and copywriting tools were used to refine age-appropriate phrasing, structure the narrative flow, and ensure compliance with the challenge constraints.

Standard personal computers and mobile devices for research, script drafting, visual layout, and slide assembly where used. No custom coding languages were required as the project focuses on accessible digital storytelling.
projectRefs: What Have Humans Left on the Moon? Artifacts and Waste - Engineerine
